title: Tale of the Old Sharper (Português)

full_text:
An elderly sharper who had spent forty years swindling merchants across the Levant retired to a quiet village near Damascus, his hair white and his knees trembling. Sitting upon his porch in the evening sun, he reflected on his past life: he had amassing gold, but had no real friends, lived in constant dread of magistrates, and his heart was empty.

One afternoon, an honest merchant dropped a heavy purse containing a thousand dinars in the dust before the old man’s gate.

The former sharper picked up the purse: forty years of habit whispered: 'Keep it!'

The old man looked at his wrinkled hands and said to his soul: 'Shall I meet my Creator with stolen gold in my fist?'

He ran after the merchant, called him back, and handed him the purse intact.

The astonished merchant rewarded him with a hundred dinars and embraced him with tears of gratitude: 'You are an angel of honesty, father!'

The old man wept with pure joy: 'For forty years I took gold by fraud, and tasted only fear; today, for the first time, I returned gold in honesty, and tasted the sweetness of a peaceful soul.' He lived his remaining years in honored peace.
moral: An old trickster learns that peaceful honesty in his twilight years is worth more than all his swindles. [PT]
